Getting started

Slamhaus is a native C++17 command-line compiler. Choose a release binary when you want to make a site quickly; compile from source when you are contributing to Slamhaus or want to work on the compiler itself.

Option 1: download a release binary

Download the latest package for your platform from the Slamhaus releases page. The release workflow publishes packages for Linux and Windows when a version tag is created.

After extracting the package, put the slamhaus executable on your PATH. On Linux, a user-local install might look like this:

mkdir -p "$HOME/.local/bin"
install -m 755 slamhaus "$HOME/.local/bin/slamhaus"
slamhaus --version

On Windows, place slamhaus.exe in a directory on PATH, or invoke it from the extracted directory. The package also contains the public <slam/slam.hpp> SDK header for C++ editor indexing and WebAssembly projects.

Option 2: compile from source

Clone the repository and configure a Release build with CMake. A C++17 compiler, CMake, and a working standard library are required.

git clone https://github.com/bitboyb/Slamhaus.git
cd Slamhaus
cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
cmake --build build --parallel
cmake --install build --prefix "$HOME/.local"
slamhaus --version

For a development build with tests enabled:

cmake -S . -B build -DBUILD_TESTING=ON
cmake --build build --parallel
ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure

If you are changing the parser, compiler, SDK, or runtime, follow the full verification commands in AGENTS.md.

Create your first site

The initializer creates a small universal project:

slamhaus init my-site
cd my-site
slamhaus check --strict
slamhaus build
slamhaus serve

Open the local address printed by slamhaus serve. The generated site is in dist/ and can be copied to a static host, object store, CDN, or GitHub Pages.

Use .md for portable GFM content. Use .slam when a page needs Slam UI, front-matter behavior, or an executable cpp wasm fence.

Add C++ browser behavior

Install the pinned Emscripten toolchain only when a page actually needs WebAssembly:

slamhaus toolchain install
slamhaus build my-site

The live showcase demonstrates the complete shape: named controls, typed event bindings, readable C++, generated output, and a small game-like interaction.

Validate before shipping 

slamhaus check my-site --strict
slamhaus fmt my-site --check
slamhaus build my-site

For editor integration, run slamhaus lsp; for shell completion, use slamhaus completion bash, zsh, or fish. Use slamhaus doctor when a compiler or Emscripten installation needs diagnosis.

Deploy the generated site

The preferred deployment path is to build locally and publish the committed dist/ directory. For this repository:

./scripts/build-pages.sh
git add dist
git commit -m "Regenerate site"
git push

The optional GitHub Actions rebuild is useful for verification, but committed output is the recommended release path because it matches the site tested locally and avoids requiring the toolchain in the deployment job.
